program_educational_objectives.description: Achieve success in industry, technical profession and/or higher education with a strong foundation in mathematics, basic sciences, applied biology and engineering fundamentals.

Implement the proficient scientific knowledge in biological sciences coupled with an engineering expertise to comprehend, analyze, design and create novel products and solutions to biological problems that are technically sound, economically feasible and socially acceptable.

Exhibit professionalism, ethical attitude, communication skills, team work in their profession, multidisciplinary approach and excellent leadership for promoting science, technology and social development for the benefit of mankind.

programme_outcomes.title: Engineering knowledge
programme_outcomes.description: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.

programme_outcomes.title: Problem analysis
programme_outcomes.description: Identify, formulate, research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

programme_outcomes.title: Design/development of solutions
programme_outcomes.description: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

programme_outcomes.title: Investigation
programme_outcomes.description: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

programme_outcomes.title: Modern tool usage
programme_outcomes.description: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

programme_outcomes.title: Engineer and society
programme_outcomes.description: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Environment and sustainability
programme_outcomes.description: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

programme_outcomes.title: Ethics
programme_outcomes.description: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

programme_outcomes.title: Individual and team work
programme_outcomes.description: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

programme_outcomes.title: Communication
programme_outcomes.description: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

programme_outcomes.title: Project management and finance
programme_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one's own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

programme_outcomes.title: Life-long learning
programme_outcomes.description: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

programme_specific_outcomes.description: Apply the knowledge to formulate, analyze and comprehend biotechnology problems which are of paramount significance in health, food processing, and agricultural sectors.
Conceive, Design and Manipulate biological systems to produce products that improve healthcare, medicine, agriculture, food, pharmaceuticals and the environment.
Develop the capacity to become independent thinker for carrying out any challenging project in the field of biotechnology.

effort_notation.T: Tutorial – 50 min per unit (marked * = optional, can be replaced by self-study)
effort_notation.O: Outside class / self-study – 1 hour per unit

semester_plan.notes: Activity Points minimum 20 required by end of Semester 4.
Activity Points minimum 40 required by end of Semester 6.
Activity Points minimum 80 required by end of Semester 8.

courses.title: Project-Part-III / Programme Elective-3 and Programme Elective-4
courses.note: Students choose one of: Project-Part-III (0L/0T/12P/6O, 6 credits) or two Programme Electives (6L/0T/0P, 6 credits total)

institute_core.title: Mathematics I
course_outcomes: CO1: Formulate some engineering problems as ODEs and hence solve such problems.
CO2: Solve linear ODEs with constant coefficients.
CO3: Find the limits, check for continuity and differentiability of real valued functions of two variables.
CO4: Test for the convergence of sequences and series.
CO5: Find the Fourier series representing periodic functions.
topics: Existence and uniqueness of solution of first order ODE, methods of solutions, linear ODE, orthogonal trajectories
Linear homogeneous second order ODEs with constant coefficients, Wronskian, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Euler-Cauchy equations
Applications of first and second order ODEs, systems of linear ODEs with constant coefficients
Functions of several variables: Limit, continuity, partial derivatives, gradient, Lagrange multipliers, Taylor's formula
Parameterised curves in space, arc length, curvature and torsion
Sequences, series, convergence tests, power series, Taylor series
Periodic functions and Fourier series, Fourier integral, Fourier transforms and properties
references: H. Anton, I. Bivens and S. Davis, Calculus, 10th Edn., John Wiley & Sons, 2015
G. B. Thomas, M. D. Weir and J. Hass, Thomas' Calculus, 12th Edn., Pearson Education, 2015
E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edn., John Wiley & Sons, 2015
Apostol, Calculus Vol 1, 1st Edn., Wiley, 2014

institute_core.title: Mathematics II
course_outcomes: CO1: Find the parametric representation of curves and surfaces in space and evaluate integrals over curves and surfaces.
CO2: Use Laplace transform and its properties to solve differential equations and integral equations.
CO3: Test the consistency of the system of linear equations and solve it.
CO4: Diagonalise symmetric matrices and use it to find the nature of quadratic forms.
topics: Vector field, divergence, curl, scalar potential, line integral, Green's theorem, double/triple integrals, Jacobian
Surface area and surface integral, flux, Gauss' divergence theorem, Stokes' theorem
Laplace transform, inverse Laplace transform, Dirac delta function, shifting theorems, convolution, solution of ODEs and integral equations
System of linear equations, Gauss elimination, LU decomposition, rank, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, Cayley-Hamilton theorem
Diagonalisation, quadratic form, reduction to canonical form
references: E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 10th Edn., Wiley, 2015
H. Anton, I. Bivens and S. Davis, Calculus, 10th Edn., John Wiley & Sons, 2015
V. I. Arnold, Ordinary Differential Equations, Springer, 2006
P. Dyke, An Introduction to Laplace Transforms and Fourier Series, Springer, 2014

institute_core.title: Mathematics III
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply the basics of probability theory in solving real life problems.
CO2: Identify the distribution and transformation of random variables.
CO3: Use techniques of statistical inference and its applications.
CO4: Apply regression and correlation for analysing real life problems.
topics: Probability distributions: Random variables, expectation, mean, variance, MGF; Binomial, Poisson, Geometric, Hypergeometric, Normal, Uniform, Gamma, Beta, Weibull distributions
Transformation of random variables, jointly distributed random variables, marginal and conditional distributions, bivariate normal distribution
Statistical inference: sampling distributions, point estimation, MLE, method of moments, interval estimation, hypothesis testing
Analysis of variance: completely randomized designs, randomized block design
Regression and correlation: curve fitting, least squares, simple regression, correlation coefficient, curvilinear regression
references: S. Ross, A First Course in Probability, 9th Edn., Pearson, 2014
R. A. Johnson, Miller and Freund's Probability and Statistics for Engineers, 8th Edn., PHI, 2011
W. W. Hines et al., Probability and Statistics for Engineering, 4th Edn., John Wiley & Sons, 2003
S. M. Ross, Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists, 5th Edn., Academic Press, 2014

institute_core.title: Mathematics IV
institute_core.note: Credits listed as 4 in syllabus; semester plan total implies 3. Source document discrepancy.
course_outcomes: CO1: Model managerial problems in industries to linear programming problems and solve them using various techniques and algorithms.
CO2: Model and solve PDEs using analytic methods.
CO3: Solve linear and nonlinear equations using numerical methods.
CO4: Evaluate definite integrals and solve ODEs using numerical methods.
topics: Linear Programming: formulation, graphical method, Simplex method, duality theory, dual simplex method
Partial Differential Equations: Cauchy's problem, Charpit's method, wave equation, heat equation, Laplace equation
Separation of variables, Fourier series, D'Alembert's solution, Laplace transforms for PDEs
Numerical methods: fixed point iteration, Regula-Falsi, Newton-Raphson, Gauss-Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel
Numerical integration: composite trapezoidal and Simpson's methods; Euler, Runge-Kutta, Adams' methods for ODEs
references: G. Mohan and K. Deep, Optimization Techniques, New Age International Publishers, 2009
W. Winston, Operations Research – Applications and Algorithms, 4th Edn., Cengage Learning, 2011
D. Greenspan, Introduction to Partial Differential Equations, Dover Publications, 2000
E. Kreyszig, Advanced Engineering Mathematics, 9th Edn., John Wiley and Sons, 2012
Jain M. K., Iyengar S. R. K., Jain R. K., Numerical Methods for Scientific and Engineering Computation, 8th Edn., New Age International, 2022

institute_core.title: Biology for Engineers
course_outcomes: CO1: Explain the evolutionary basis of life and the structure-function relationship of biomolecules.
CO2: Describe the characteristics of the cellular composition, communication, and principles of genetics.
CO3: Evaluate and apply the biological principles to solve real-world problems related to food, agriculture, and environmental sciences.
CO4: Illustrate biocatalysis and the basic concepts in energy transformation.
topics: Origin of life, Darwinian Evolution, biomolecule structure and function (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids), central dogma
Cell structure and function, signal transduction, cell division, Mendelian genetics, chromosomal aberrations
Enzymes: classification, catalysis, kinetics, inhibition; basic concepts in energy transformation and photosynthesis
Human diseases, biosensors, vaccines, antibiotics, genetic modification of crops, bioremediation, biofuels
references: L. A. Urry et al., Campbell Biology, 11th Edn., Pearson Education, 2017
S. Thyagarajan et al., Biology for Engineers, McGraw Hill Education, 2013
W. S. Klug et al., Concepts of Genetics, Global Edn., Pearson, 2019
D. L. Nelson and M. M. Cox, Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, Macmillan Learning, 2021
S. I. Fox, Human Physiology, 13th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2011
A. G. Webb, Principles of Biomedical Instrumentation, Cambridge University Press, 2018
A. T. Johnson, Biology for Engineers, CRC Press, 2018

institute_core.title: General Chemistry
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply the concepts of acid-base chemistry to bioactive molecules.
CO2: Demonstrate the principles of stereochemistry for organic synthesis.
CO3: Construct the fundamental concepts of reaction mechanisms in synthetic chemistry.
CO4: Utilize the basic concepts of essential metal ions in biological systems.
topics: Acid-Base Chemistry: Bronsted and Lewis acids/bases, aqueous and non-aqueous systems, acids and bases of biological interest
Stereochemistry: basic concepts, stereochemical descriptors, enantiomers, diastereomers, stereoselective and stereospecific reactions
Reaction mechanisms: electrophilic and nucleophilic substitution, carbocations, leaving group effects, steric effects
Biological reactions mediated by enzymes: group transfer, carbon-carbon double bond formation, isomerization, hydrolysis, oxidation-reduction
Heterocyclic chemistry: nomenclature, importance in medicinal chemistry
Essential and trace metal ions in biology, bio-ligands, enzyme classification and kinetics
Chemical hazards and toxic substances
references: E. V. Anslyn and D. A. Dougherty, Modern Physical Organic Chemistry, University Science Books, 2005
R. Chang, General Chemistry: The Essential Concepts, 5th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2008
E. L. Eliel and S. H. Wilen, Stereochemistry of Organic Compounds, Wiley, 1994
L. G. Wade Jr., Organic Chemistry, 8th Edn., Pearson Education, 2013
J. E. Huheey et al., Inorganic Chemistry – Principles of Structure and Reactivity, Pearson India Ltd., 2009
S. J. Lippard and J. M. Berg, Principles of Bioinorganic Chemistry, University Science Books, 1994

institute_core.title: Professional Communication
course_outcomes: CO1: Distinguish the role and purpose of communication at the workplace and for academic purposes.
CO2: Decide strategies and modes for effective communication in a dynamic workplace.
CO3: Combine multiple approaches for successful and ethical information exchange.
CO4: Estimate best communication practices to assist productivity and congeniality at the workplace.
topics: Listening and reading comprehension: introductions, feedback, public speaking, note-taking from lectures
Vocabulary and speaking: professional vocabulary, sentence structures, critical reading, text appreciation
Effective writing: note-making, paragraph writing, official letters, emails, abstract writing
Communication at workplace: theory, modes, verbal/nonverbal, group discussions, presentations, digital etiquette, ethical communication
references: N. Bhatnagar, Communicative English for Engineers and Professionals, Pearson Education India, 2010
B. A. Garner, HBR Guide to Better Business Writing, Harvard Business Review Press, 2013
S. Kumar and P. Lata, Communication Skills, Oxford University Press, 2011

institute_core.title: Professional Ethics
course_outcomes: CO1: Develop a clear understanding of human values and use it as the basis for all the activities.
CO2: Understand and follow the ethical aspects of the engineering profession.

CO3: Align with the Code of Ethics prescribed by the Society for Biological Engineering (AIChE), Department of Biotechnology and Indian Council of Medical Research, Govt of India in all professional activities.
CO4: Assimilate the elements of academic integrity and Honour Codes, and adopt them in all relevant activities.
topics: Human Values: morals, integrity, work ethic, civic virtue, honesty, empathy, self-confidence
Ethics in Professional Practice: ethical basis of engineering, responsibilities to consumers, safety, IP management, environmental sustainability
Code of Ethics: Society for Biological Engineering (AIChE), DBT and ICMR guidelines
Academic Integrity: honesty, trust, fairness, plagiarism, Honour Codes
references: R. S. Naagarazan, A Textbook on Professional Ethics and Human Values, 3rd Edn., New Age International, 2022
A. F. Bainbridge, Ethics for Engineers: A Brief Introduction, CRC Press, 2021
Handbook for Institutional Biosafety Committee, Dept. of Biotechnology, Govt of India (2017 & 2020)
National guidelines for stem cell research, DBT and ICMR, 2017
National ethical guidelines for biomedical and health research involving human participants, ICMR, 2017

programme_core.title: Unit Operations
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe the basic concepts and equations in fluid mechanics, heat transfer and vapor liquid equilibrium.
CO2: Illustrate the design of equipment used for flow measurement, heat exchange, evaporation, distillation and mechanical operations.
CO3: Analyze and solve a variety of problems in fluid statics, fluid dynamics, heat transfer and mass transfer.
CO4: Identify the relationship between physical quantities and develop equations to solve complex problems.
topics: Fluid mechanics: fluid classification, Newton's law of viscosity, Pascal's law, Bernoulli equation, Hagen-Poiseuille equation, dimensional analysis
Flow measurements: orifice meter, venturimeter; pumps; size reduction; sedimentation; mixing
Heat transfer: conduction (Fourier's law), convection, heat exchangers, evaporation (single and multiple effect)
Mass transfer: Fick's law, diffusion, distillation (McCabe-Thiele method), drying
references: W. L. McCabe, J. Smith and P. Harriott, Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering, 7th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2017
R. K. Rajput, A Textbook of Fluid Mechanics, S. Chand & Company, 2019
J. M. Coulson and J. F. Richardson, Chemical Engineering, Vol. IA, 7th Edn., Butterworth-Heinemann, 2017
J. P. Holman, Heat Transfer, 8th Edn., McGraw Hill, 2010

programme_core.title: Microbiology
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify the microbial diversity and apply basic knowledge to culture, enumerate, visualize, and classify different types of microorganisms.
CO2: Explain the structure, reproduction of bacteria, fungi, and viruses and demonstrate their growth control.
CO3: Describe both aerobic and anaerobic microbial metabolic processes.
CO4: Assess the beneficial and harmful effects of microbes in medical, industrial, agricultural and environmental microbiology.
topics: General Microbiology: prokaryotes and eukaryotes, viruses, bacteria, fungi, algae, protozoa; staining techniques; microscopy; control methods
Microbial Physiology: nutritional requirements, growth curve, culture and enumeration, biochemical and molecular characterization
Microbial Genetics and Metabolism: genetics of viruses and bacteria; aerobic and anaerobic processes; photophosphorylation; secondary metabolism
Medical, Environmental, Industrial and Agricultural Microbiology: infections, antibiotic resistance, industrial and environmental applications
references: J. Willey, L. Sherwood and C. J. Woolverton, Prescott's Microbiology, 11th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2021
M. J. Pelczar, E. C. S. Chan and N. R. Krieg, Microbiology, 5th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2021
G. J. Tortora, B. R. Funke and C. L. Case, Microbiology: An Introduction, 13th Edn., Addison-Wesley, 2018
M. Madigan et al., Brock Biology of Microorganisms, 16th Edn., Pearson, 2020

programme_core.title: Biochemistry
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe the genetic, chemical and physical fundamentals of biochemistry.
CO2: Explain the importance of biomolecules and apply their structural basis to perceive the biological functions.
CO3: Interpret the bioenergetic principles behind the metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.
CO4: Analyze the biosynthetic pathway for synthesis of different biological macromolecules.
topics: Fundamentals: cellular, chemical, physical, genetic foundations; water interactions; Henderson-Hasselbalch equation
Biological Macromolecular Structures: proteins (amino acids to quaternary structure), carbohydrates, nucleotides and nucleic acids, lipids, hormones
Cellular Metabolism and Bioenergetics: glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, TCA cycle, fatty acid oxidation, urea cycle, oxidative phosphorylation
Biosynthesis of Macromolecules: carbohydrate, lipid, amino acid and nucleotide biosynthesis
references: D. L. Nelson and M. M. Cox, Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, Macmillan Learning, 2021
J. M. Berg, J. L. Tymoczko and L. Stryer, Biochemistry, Macmillan, 2007
D. Voet, J. G. Voet and C. W. Pratt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry, John Wiley & Sons, 2016
V. W. Rodwell et al., Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, McGraw-Hill, 2018

programme_core.title: Microbiology Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Practice different standard Microbiology Lab practices and apply proper practices in appropriate situations.
CO2: Apply basic knowledge of preparation of different types of culture media and sterilization techniques.
CO3: Demonstrate techniques of staining, culturing, isolation, identification, enumeration, storage and preservation of microbes.
CO4: Design an experimental setup for the detection of bacterial products of industrial and agricultural importance.
lab_topics: Preparation of culture media (broth and agar)
Isolation of pure culture (streak plate and pour plate)
Isolation of microbes from soil/mouth flora/water
Identification by staining, biochemical testing and antibiotic sensitivity
Isolation of microbes from milk and fermented food
Detection of microbial products – acids and enzymes

programme_core.title: Biochemistry Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply theoretical knowledge and demonstrate proficiency to design, execute, and analyze experiments in biochemistry.
CO2: Perform a variety of biochemical assays, and analyze and interpret biochemical data.
CO3: Develop experimental skills and understand the importance of good laboratory practice in biochemistry.
CO4: Communicate scientific findings effectively through reports and presentations.
lab_topics: Introduction to Biochemistry Laboratory: safety, spectrophotometry, pH measurements, buffer preparation
Qualitative tests for carbohydrates and amino acids
Separation of proteins by SDS-PAGE electrophoresis

programme_core.title: Cell Biology and Genetics
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe the characteristics of the cell and composition, cell organelles structure, and function.
CO2: Illustrate the cell cycle regulation and second messengers involved in cellular signaling.
CO3: Explain the Mendelian genetics, linkage, and crossing over.
CO4: Apply the concepts of genetics to understanding the inheritance of genetic diseases and molecular tools to analyze them.
CO5: Apply the knowledge of cell biology in experiments for the visualization of stained and unstained cells and their organelles.
topics: Cell structure and nuclear function: cell theory, prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, membrane structure, transport mechanisms, nuclear envelope, chromosomes
Cell organelles, cell cycle and signaling: mitochondria, ER, Golgi, lysosomes; mitosis, meiosis; cyclin-CDK checkpoints; G-protein coupled receptors, PI3-kinase pathway
Mendelian genetics: monohybrid and dihybrid cross, incomplete dominance, codominance, sex-linked genes, linkage, crossing over
Genetic technology and population genetics: transposable elements, gene therapy, transgenic organisms, Hardy-Weinberg principle, developmental genetics
lab_topics: Enumeration of cell count using a hemocytometer
Preparation of blood smear and differential WBC count
Staining and observation of Barr's body
Chromosome preparation and visualization by staining
references: P. Snustad and M. J. Simmons, Principles of Genetics, 7th Edn., 2015
M. R. Cummings et al., Concepts of Genetics, 12th Global Edn., 2019
J. E. Krebs et al., Lewin's GENES XII, 12th Edn., Jones and Bartlett, 2018
A. Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 5th Edn., Garland Science, 2008
H. Lodish et al., Molecular Cell Biology, 9th Edn., W. H. Freeman, 2021

programme_core.title: Process Calculations
course_outcomes: CO1: Perform unit conversion involved in bioprocesses and know the expression of the concentration of dilute solutions.
CO2: Solve the material balance problems in unit operations.
CO3: Analyze the stoichiometry of cell growth and product formation.
CO4: Solve the energy balance problems in fermentation processes.
topics: Stoichiometric Principles: unit conversion, dimensional consistency, mole concept, concentration, graphical differentiation and integration
Material Balance: general equation for steady and unsteady state, element balance, material balance in crystallization, drying, distillation, recycle, bypass and purge calculations
Stoichiometry of Bioprocesses: cell growth and product formation, elemental balances, yield coefficients, maintenance coefficients, oxygen consumption
Energy Balance: heat capacity, enthalpy calculations, heat of combustion, energy balance for fermentation
references: K. V. Narayanan and B. Lakshmikuttyamma, Stoichiometry & Process Calculations, Prentice Hall, 2006
B. I. Bhatt and S. M. Vora, Stoichiometry, 4th Edn., Tata McGraw-Hill, 2001
M. L. Shuler and F. Kargi, Bioprocess Engineering – Basic Concepts, 2nd Edn., Prentice Hall, 2004
P. M. Doran, Bioprocess Engineering Principles, 2nd Edn., Academic Press, 2005

programme_core.title: Environmental Bioengineering
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify the fundamental concepts and principles of ecology and ecosystems.
CO2: Analyze the impact of air and noise pollution on the environment and human health.
CO3: Evaluate sources and classification of water pollutants and sewage/wastewater treatment.
CO4: Apply biotechnological methods to assess pollution control: biodegradation, bioremediation, phytoremediation, waste management.
topics: Ecology and Ecosystem: ecosystem balance, diversity indices, thermodynamics, food energy chains
Air and Noise Pollution: sources, monitoring, control, Ambient Air Quality, Air Act 1981, decibel, noise measurement
Water Pollution: classification of pollutants, sewage treatment, activated sludge, nitrification-denitrification, waste stabilization ponds
Biotechnological Methods: biodegradation, bioremediation, phytoremediation, E-waste management
references: E. P. Odum, Fundamentals of Ecology, 5th Edn., Brooks/Cole, 2004
G. Tchobanoglous, F. Burton and Stensel, Wastewater Engineering, 4th Edn., Tata McGraw Hill, 2008
C. S. Rao, Environmental Pollution Control Engineering, New Age International, 2021
B. C. Bhattacharyya and R. Banerjee, Environmental Biotechnology, Oxford University Press, 2007

programme_core.title: Bioprocess Engineering
course_outcomes: CO1: Design a fermentation process in a bioreactor.
CO2: Analyze the cell growth and product formation in different cultivation systems.
CO3: Design batch and continuous sterilization.
CO4: Perform modeling and simulation of bioprocess.
topics: Fermentation and Bioreactor: fermentation types, media design and optimization, bioreactor configuration, control of pH/temperature/DO
Cultivation Systems and Oxygen Transfer: Monod model, batch/continuous/fed-batch cultivation, mass transfer, Kla
Design of Sterilization: thermal death kinetics, batch and continuous sterilization, filter and air sterilization, effluent treatment
Modeling and Simulation: structured and non-structured models, dynamic simulation, immobilized enzyme reactors
references: J. E. Bailey and D. F. Ollis, Biochemical Engineering Fundamentals, 2nd Edn., McGraw Hill, 2017
M. L. Shuler and F. Kargi, Bioprocess Engineering – Basic Concepts, 2nd Edn., Prentice Hall, 2015
P. M. Doran, Bioprocess Engineering Principles, 2nd Edn., Academic Press, 2005
P. F. Stanbury, S. J. Hall and A. Whitaker, Principles of Fermentation Technology, 3rd Edn., Elsevier, 2016

programme_core.title: Molecular Biology and Genetic Engineering
course_outcomes: CO1: Comprehend the concepts of DNA as genetic material, genes and associated phenotypes.
CO2: Analyze central dogma of transmission of genetic information.
CO3: Develop the concept of gene regulation and genetic recombination.
CO4: Evaluate and analyze cloning of DNA fragments and its modifications.
CO5: Generate synthetic DNA molecules, construct and evaluate synthetic organisms.
topics: DNA as genetic material, epigenetics, central dogma, DNA replication in prokaryotes and eukaryotes
Transcription and post-transcriptional processing; translation and post-translational modifications
Gene regulation: operon model (lac, gal, trp); DNA damage and repair; transposons; retroviruses; homologous recombination
Recombinant DNA technology: restriction enzymes, plasmids, cosmids, cloning vectors, expression vectors, hybridization
DNA sequencing, PCR variants, DNA fingerprinting, site-directed mutagenesis, RFLP, CRISPR
references: R. Weaver, Molecular Biology, 5th Edn., McGraw-Hill, 2018
J. D. Watson et al., Molecular Biology of the Gene, 7th Edn., Pearson, 2013
J. E. Krebs et al., Lewin's GENES XII, 12th Edn., Jones and Bartlett, 2017
D. S. T. Nicholl, An Introduction to Genetic Engineering, 4th Edn., Cambridge University Press, 2023

programme_core.title: Bioprocess Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Perform the kinetics of fermentation processes.
CO2: Design and optimize medium components for biomass production.
CO3: Analyze the oxygen transfer rate in fermentation processes.
CO4: Execute small scale and pilot scale study for fermentation of biological products.
lab_topics: Growth curve of bacteria – specific growth rate, yield coefficient, product formation kinetics
Control of pH and temperature in a bioprocess
Control of flow rates and pressure
Enzyme immobilization and whole cell immobilization
Determination of Kla by static gassing out and sulphite oxidation
Mixing time in stirred tank reactor with Newtonian and Non-Newtonian fluids
Measurement of ethanol production in a fermentor

programme_core.title: Molecular Biology Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Prepare DNA and RNA from any biological sources.
CO2: Generate and analyze the restriction pattern of DNA molecules.
CO3: Transform yeast and bacteria with plasmid DNA for phenotypic analysis.
CO4: Amplify DNA fragment and evaluate.
CO5: Design, comprehend and assess any DNA molecules.
lab_topics: Isolation of plasmid from E. coli
Transformation of E. coli and yeast
Isolation of genomic DNA from eukaryotes
PCR of a gene from genomic DNA
Cloning PCR product into a vector
Restriction mapping of a cloned DNA fragment
Isolation of DNA fragments by restriction digestion and gel elution
Cloning of isolated DNA fragment into a plasmid
Isolation of mRNA and cDNA synthesis
Gene expression analysis using Real-Time PCR
Site directed mutagenesis of a cloned gene

programme_core.title: Bioinformatics
course_outcomes: CO1: Utilize the available online biological databases to retrieve and analyze sequences.
CO2: Analyze the basic algorithms for sequence analysis of proteins and nucleic acids.
CO3: Develop an idea about predictive methods for structure and function of nucleic acid and protein sequences.
CO4: Apply bioinformatics approaches to solve biological problems such as gene annotation, molecular evolution and drug designing.
CO5: Critically evaluate the results of bioinformatics analyses and their biological significance.
topics: Introduction to Bioinformatics and Biological Databases: Genbank, NCBI, DDBJ, Pubmed, UniProt, PROSITE, SCOP, RCSB-PDB, EMBL-EBI, STRING, TCGA
Sequence Alignment: substitution matrices (PAM, BLOSUM), gap penalties, Needleman-Wunsch, Smith-Waterman, FASTA, BLAST, CLUSTALX, HMM
Phylogenetic Analysis: substitution models, evaluating phylogenetic trees
Structure Prediction and Analysis: protein homology modeling, drug discovery, protein-protein interactions
Data Analysis: NGS, SNP detection, gene prediction, microarray data analysis
references: A. K. Lesk, Introduction to Bioinformatics, 5th Edn., Oxford University Press, 2019
J. Pevsner, Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics, 3rd Edn., Wiley-Blackwell, 2015
D. W. Mount, Bioinformatics: Sequence and Genome Analysis, 2nd Edn., Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press, 2004

programme_core.title: Downstream Process Engineering
course_outcomes: CO1: Recognize the basis for various steps in downstream processing and their economics, to design a purification strategy.
CO2: Apply basic laws governing downstream processing unit operations to solve practical problems.
CO3: Assess techniques such as precipitation, membrane separation and chromatography for purification.
CO4: Propose a technique to give final polishing to the isolated product.
topics: Introduction to downstream processing: economics, cost-cutting strategies, process design for different classes of bioproducts
Primary Separation and Recovery: cell disruption, centrifugation, filtration, flocculation, sedimentation
Enrichment Operations: extraction, aqueous two-phase extraction, adsorption, precipitation, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, dialysis
Fractionation and Polishing: chromatographic techniques (adsorption, ion exchange, affinity, gel filtration, HPLC), crystallization, drying
references: N. K. Prasad, Downstream Process Technology, PHI, 2012
M. R. Ladisch, Bioseparations Engineering, Wiley Interscience, 2001
J. D. Seader and E. J. Henley, Separation Process Principles, 3rd Edn., Wiley, 2010
P. A. Belter, E. L. Cussler and W. S. Hu, Bioseparation: Downstream Processing for Biotechnology, 2nd Edn., Wiley, 1994

programme_core.title: Biopharmaceutical Technology
course_outcomes: CO1: Examine the growth of biopharmaceutical industries and recent pharmaceutical molecules.
CO2: Analyze the evolution of biopharmaceutical product development and identify key sources of biopharmaceuticals.
CO3: Apply the principles of drug formulation, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics for designing and developing new drugs.
CO4: Evaluate and design novel steps involved in industrial production and purification of biopharmaceuticals.
topics: Introduction to Biopharmaceutical Industries: small molecules, biologics, biogenerics, biosimilars; world and Indian scenario
Drug Discovery and Development: ADME, pharmacodynamics, clinical trials, GMP, regulatory approvals (USFDA, CDSCO)
Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics: compartment models, bioavailability, drug-receptor interactions, dose-response relationships
Case Studies: cytokines, hormones, monoclonal antibodies, cell therapy (CAR-T, stem cell), gene therapy, vaccines
references: M. E. Aulton and K. Taylor (Eds.), Aulton's Pharmaceutics, Elsevier Health Sciences, 2013
T. N. Tozer and M. Rowland, Essentials of Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics, Wolters Kluwer, 2016
I. Ramzan (Ed.), Biologics, Biosimilars, and Biobetters, John Wiley & Sons, 2020

programme_core.title: Bioinformatics Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Utilize online databases and basic algorithms for nucleic acid and protein sequence analysis.
CO2: Demonstrate predictive methods for protein structure, function, and phylogenetic relatedness.
CO3: Analyze and compare nucleic acid and protein sequences.
CO4: Apply protein-protein interactions and microarray data analysis for experimental design.
CO5: Develop hypotheses based on bioinformatics data and design experiments to test them.
lab_topics: Basics of sequence analysis, retrieving nucleic acid/protein sequences
Secondary and tertiary structure prediction of proteins
Identification of functional sites in genes and genomes

programme_core.title: Downstream Process Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply principles of cell disruption, filtration, concentration, extraction and drying and analyze efficiency.
CO2: Plan and evaluate downstream processing steps for expression and purification of a recombinant protein.
CO3: Design experimental setups to isolate proteins/enzymes and small molecules using precipitation and chromatography.
lab_topics: Solid-liquid separation by filtration, sedimentation and flocculation
Separation of small molecules from macromolecules by ultrafiltration and dialysis
Aqueous two-phase extraction and batch extraction
Separation of carbohydrates/amino acids by TLC
Downstream processing of a recombinant protein from a bacterial system
Ammonium sulphate precipitation of recombinant protein
Downstream processing of lysozyme by ion exchange chromatography
Gel filtration chromatography for salt removal
Downstream processing of citric acid (Aspergillus spp.)
Downstream processing of caffeine from tea dust
Product polishing by lyophilisation and drying

programme_core.title: Analytical Techniques and Instrumentation
course_outcomes: CO1: Analyse and identify suitable analytical techniques for quantification of biological macromolecules.
CO2: Apply the working principles of electrophoretic, spectroscopic, chromatographic and microscopic techniques for molecular characterisation.
CO3: Interpret data procured from molecular characterization and provide structural and functional details.
CO4: Design series of experiments involving various techniques for purification and analysis of proteins, lipids, DNA and carbohydrates.
topics: Electrophoretic Techniques: gel electrophoresis (DNA and proteins), isoelectric focusing, 2D-PAGE, PFGE, Western/Southern blot
Spectroscopic Techniques: UV-Vis, fluorescence/phosphorescence, atomic absorption, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy
Chromatography and Structure Analysis: GC, HPLC, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry (LC/MS, GC/MS), XRD, NMR, circular dichroism
Microscopic Techniques: phase contrast, fluorescence, electron (SEM, TEM, Cryo-EM), confocal, super-resolution, AFM
references: K. Wilson et al. (Eds.), Wilson and Walker's Principles and Techniques of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Cambridge University Press, 2018
W. W. Parson and C. Burda, Modern Optical Spectroscopy, Springer, 2022
V. Ramesh (Ed.), Biomolecular and Bioanalytical Techniques, John Wiley & Sons, 2019

programme_core.title: Immunotechnology
course_outcomes: CO1: Explain different molecules, cells and tissues of the vertebrate immune system and the cooperation between innate and adaptive immunity.
CO2: Discuss and compare the innate and adaptive immune response mechanisms in physiological and pathological states.
CO3: Apply the knowledge of antigen-antibody interactions for the development of novel immunodiagnostic techniques.
CO4: Develop novel therapy for human diseases by applying biotechnological principles in immunology.
topics: Cellular and Molecular Components: innate and acquired immunity, antibody structure, MHC, complement system
Immune Response Mechanisms: B and T lymphocyte maturation, humoral and cell-mediated responses, cytokines, ADCC
Immune System Dysfunction and Immunodiagnostics: hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, immunodeficiency; RIA, ELISA, immunoblotting, flow cytometry
Immunotherapeutics: hybridoma technology, monoclonal antibodies, vaccines (mRNA, vector, subunit), immunosuppressive therapies
references: J. Punt et al., Kuby Immunology, 8th Edn., W. H. Freeman, 2018
K. M. Murphy et al., Janeway's Immunobiology, 10th Edn., W. W. Norton, 2022
A. K. Abbas et al., Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 10th Edn., Elsevier, 2021

programme_core.title: Biosafety and Bioethics
course_outcomes: CO1: Define ethical values in scientific research and ethical violations.
CO2: Analyze the biological, chemical, physical, and radioactive laboratory hazards and their prevention and safety measures.
CO3: Apply the concepts and ethical guidelines to carry out research in genetic engineering, animal, human, and stem cell research.
CO4: Summarize the national and international guidelines and policies for good laboratory practices and biosafety.
topics: Responsible Conduct of Science: values in science, misconduct, plagiarism, IP rights, authorship, research with humans/animals/stem cells
Laboratory Safety: biohazards, biosafety cabinets, biosafety levels 1-4, chemical/radiation/electrical/fire safety, bio-waste segregation
Guidelines for Stem Cells and GMOs: Institutional Biosafety Committee compliance, containment and storage of GMOs
Ethics in Animal and Human Research: CCSEA guidelines, ICMR guidelines, institutional ethics committee responsibilities
references: Handbook for Institutional Biosafety Committee, Dept. of Biotechnology, Govt of India (2017 & 2020)
Laboratory Biosafety Manual, 4th Edn., World Health Organization, 2020
National guidelines for stem cell research, DBT and ICMR, 2017
National ethical guidelines for biomedical and health research, ICMR, 2017

programme_core.title: Immunology Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Investigate antigen-antibody interactions and apply the knowledge to diagnostic immunology.
CO2: Explain the methods of studying immune reactions.
CO3: Apply the principle of western blotting and demonstrate the presence of specific protein molecules.
lab_topics: qRT-PCR based immune cell gene expression assay

programme_core.title: Plant Biotechnology
course_outcomes: CO1: Describe the basic concepts and principles of plant tissue culture and its application.
CO2: Evaluate different methods of plant transformation.
CO3: Assess the state-of-the-art techniques used in plant biotechnology.
CO4: Identify the biotechnological applications and metabolic pathways in plants.
topics: Plant Tissue Culture: media composition, sterilization, totipotency, micropropagation, somatic embryogenesis, protoplast culture, cryopreservation
Tissue Culture Applications: haploid production, germplasm conservation, secondary metabolites, bioreactor systems
Plant Transformation Technology: Agrobacterium-mediated gene transfer, Ti/Ri plasmids, binary vectors, biolistics, transgene silencing
Secondary Metabolite Pathways and Applications: shikimate, phenylpropanoid, terpenoid pathways; biopesticides, biofuels, nutraceuticals, GMO commercialization
references: C. N. Stewart Jr, Plant Biotechnology and Genetics, John Wiley & Sons, 2016
S. Umesha, Plant Biotechnology, 2nd Edn., CRC Press, 2019
A. Slater, N. Scott and M. R. Fowler, Plant Biotechnology: The Genetic Manipulation of Plants, 2nd Edn., Oxford University Press, 2008

programme_core.title: Plant Biotechnology Laboratory
course_outcomes: CO1: Acquire hands-on experience in various plant tissue culture techniques.
CO2: Demonstrate the plant regeneration processes including regeneration from seeds, vegetative multiplication and callus induction.
CO3: Demonstrate essential molecular biology techniques applicable to plant biotechnology.
lab_topics: Requirements for Plant Tissue Culture Laboratory
Sterilization technique and inoculation of various explants
Genomic DNA isolation from plant sample

programme_core.title: Project-Part-I
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply the principles of natural science, mathematics and engineering for designing experiments to solve complex problems.
CO2: Develop skills to use modern tools and equipment as an individual or team with professional and ethical commitments.
CO3: Disseminate information gained through written reports and presentations.
CO4: Plan and execute project objectives in a timely manner with appropriate financial management.
CO5: Demonstrate the ability to adapt and self-learn new techniques.
programme_core.description: Students form groups of up to four members and propose projects in consultation with faculty. Evaluated by mid-semester and end-semester committee presentations and a detailed project report.

programme_core.title: Internship
course_outcomes: CO1: Identify the layout, machinery, organizational structure and production processes in industry/research laboratory.
CO2: Implement the industrial practices and work culture as an individual, team member or leader.
CO3: Evaluate the impact of engineering solutions in a global, economic, environmental and societal context.
CO4: Communicate effectively through technical report and presentation.
programme_core.description: Students undergo training individually in reputed firms/research institutes/laboratories for 2 months. A detailed report is submitted within ten days of the commencement of the next semester.

programme_core.title: Project-Part-II
course_outcomes: CO1: Apply the principles of natural science, mathematics and engineering for designing experiments to solve complex problems.
CO2: Develop skills to use modern tools and equipment as an individual or team with professional and ethical commitments.
CO3: Disseminate information gained through written reports and presentations.
